title: OpenRouter Unified AI Model API
positioning: A unified model marketplace and API gateway for teams that need broad model access, centralized billing, provider routing, fallbacks, privacy controls, and usage observability without maintaining a separate integration for every provider.
decisionAngles: Unified integration convenience versus adding another production dependency
Automatic provider routing versus reproducible provider, latency, caching, and output behavior
Pass-through inference pricing versus credit-purchase, BYOK, and provider-specific charges
OpenRouter prompt non-logging versus downstream provider retention and training policies
Fast model experimentation versus production controls for budgets, privacy, fallbacks, and deprecations
Free model exploration versus paid capacity suitable for production workloads

pricingSnapshot.billingUnit: Inference is billed using each selected model and provider's token, request, image, or reasoning-unit price; OpenRouter currently adds a 5.5% fee when purchasing credits rather than marking up inference prices.
plans: Free: 25+ free models, four free providers, and 50 requests per day
Pay-as-you-go: no minimum spend, model-based prices, high global limits, and a 5.5% platform fee
Enterprise: volume commitments, discounted platform fees, optional dedicated limits, invoicing, SSO/SAML, policy enforcement, and support SLA
BYOK pay-as-you-go: up to USD 25,000 of list-price inference per month without a fee, then 5%; higher enterprise threshold is listed separately
volatileFields: BYOK fee-free thresholds and enterprise terms
pricingSnapshot.releaseGuard: Recheck the live pricing, FAQ, and selected model endpoint immediately before migration; do not describe a provider count, model count, or endpoint price as permanent.

policyBoundaries.label: OpenRouter privacy and downstream-provider policies are separate layers
policyBoundaries.summary: OpenRouter says prompts and completions are not logged by default, but requests are still sent to model providers whose retention, training, and endpoint policies can differ.
policyBoundaries.releaseGuard: Never summarize OpenRouter non-logging as a guarantee that every routed provider has zero retention or no training.

policyBoundaries.label: Zero Data Retention is endpoint- and feature-scoped
policyBoundaries.summary: ZDR can constrain inference routing, but endpoint policies vary, in-memory caching may still qualify as ZDR, and plugins or tools such as web search have their own policies.
policyBoundaries.releaseGuard: State the inference-routing scope and require endpoint-level verification for regulated or sensitive workloads.

policyBoundaries.label: Routing improves availability but can reduce reproducibility
policyBoundaries.summary: Default routing can move requests among providers; differences in latency, quantization, caching, supported parameters, and provider behavior can affect cost and output.
policyBoundaries.releaseGuard: Recommend explicit provider ordering, parameter requirements, fallbacks, privacy rules, and price ceilings where reproducibility matters.

limitations: Default multi-provider routing can change the serving endpoint, latency, quantization, caching behavior, and effective output characteristics unless the team pins or constrains providers.
A unified OpenAI-compatible interface does not guarantee that every model supports identical parameters, tools, structured output, context handling, or safety behavior.
OpenRouter prompt non-logging does not replace reviewing the selected provider endpoint's retention, training, residency, and compliance policy.
ZDR applies to eligible inference endpoints and does not automatically cover plugins, external tools, or every form of in-memory prompt caching.
Free models have low shared rate limits and are explicitly unsuitable for most production workloads.
Credits, purchase fees, refund windows, possible credit expiry, provider price changes, and failed or fallback request behavior require billing controls and monitoring.
Centralizing model access through OpenRouter introduces an additional account, credit balance, routing, support, and availability dependency.

marketValidation.rationale: OpenRouter has strong current scale, product breadth, independent review, and strategic validation. Its durable value is not merely listing models; it combines a unified API with routing, observability, billing, policy filters, and provider choice. The recommendation remains conditional because production teams must actively constrain privacy, provider behavior, fallback policy, and spend.
strongSignals: OpenRouter's 2026-08-19 announcement reports more than 10 trillion tokens processed per day and a community of over 10 million developers and companies
OpenRouter and Stripe both announced an agreement for OpenRouter to join Stripe on 2026-08-19
The live pricing page lists hundreds of models and dozens of providers across pay-as-you-go and enterprise access
G2 lists 21 reviews with a 4.6 rating at review time
recurringUserFriction: Provider routing and fallback choices can create cost, latency, caching, and output variance
Privacy requires both OpenRouter settings and endpoint-specific provider-policy review
Billing, account support, credit refunds, and changing model availability create operational overhead
